post.summary: Emails a sign-in link. Always accepted, whether or not the address belongs to an account.
Exchanges the single-use token from a sign-in link for a bearer token, activating an invited user.

Exchanges a refresh token for a new access token and its successor, sliding the session forward. The refresh
token supplied is spent by this call; replaying it ends the session.

Signs out by ending the session a refresh token belongs to. Succeeds even for a token that is already gone,
so a client can always clear its credentials.

get.summary: Returns the profile behind the bearer token on this request.

delete.summary: Deletes an organization along with its users.

get.summary: Returns the organization's logo, or the placeholder when it has none. Behind the bearer token like everything else here, because which organizations exist is not public. A browser cannot put a token on an ``, so a client fetches this and hands the response to the element as an object URL.

delete.summary: Removes the organization's logo, which puts it back to the placeholder.

put.summary: Sets or replaces the organization's logo, and answers with the organization.

get.summary:
Returns a page of users, optionally limited to those still invited or already active. Deleted users are left
out unless `includeDeleted` asks for them, which is how an administrator finds one to restore.
Returns a single user. Deleted users are not found here; they are listed by the roster on request.

put.summary:
Updates a user's name, email address, role and organization, as an administrator. Omitting `role` or
`organizationId` leaves that field alone, which is the whole request an organization administrator
can make: changing either is reserved to platform administrators.

delete.summary:
Deletes a user. They lose access immediately and are emailed about it; an administrator can undo this with
the restore endpoint.

post.summary: Invites someone into an organization and emails them a link that accepts the invitation and signs them in.
Sends a fresh invitation link, retiring the previous one.

Restores a deleted user, leaving one who is not deleted as they are. Their sign-in links and sessions are
not restored with them, so they sign in again from the login page.

put.summary: Updates the signed-in user's own profile. Open to any role, unlike the administrator edit below.

UpdateOrganizationRequest.description: The body of a rename request. The identifier comes from the route.

UpdateUserRequest.description:
The body of a user update. The identifier comes from the route. `Role` and `OrganizationId` are
optional and mean "leave this alone"; the fields every editor can change are always sent.

Bearer.description: Enter the access token returned by POST /api/auth/tokens.
